newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Perez Companc buys Block X oil rights.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Perez Companc buys Block X oil rights.

text.p: In an auction Tuesday, Argentina's Compania Perez Companc bought the rights to explore and develop state-run Petroperu's oil Block X for $202 million, Peruvian privatization officials said.

Perez Companc beat out four other bids from Canada's Norcen Energy Resources Ltd, China's CNPC America Peru SA, U.S. company Pennzoil Co, and a consortium 60 percent controlled by Argentina's Pluspetrol Corp and 40 percent held by Peru's Grana y Montero Petrolera SA.
Petroperu said U.S. company Petrosantander Peru SA, which had presented its technical qualifications to enter the auction, did not meet the state entity's criteria to make a bid.
The closest rival bid to Perez Companc was that of CNPC, which offered to buy the block rights for $190 million.
Petroperu had set a $65 million minimum bid for the block, which has proven reserves of 49 million barrels of crude oil and lies 720 miles (1,150 km) north of Lima in the Talara region.

The contract being offered by state oil company Petroperu includes a 30-year licence to extract oil and a 40-year licence for natural gas. The block currently produces 17,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil from its roughly 39,000 hectare area, officials said.
On winning the oil rights, Hugo Pereira, representing Perez Companc, said his company intended to invest in the block more than the minimum government requirement of $25 million over five years.
"The rate of return (on the investment) depends on the reserves," he told reporters. "It is not a large reserve. This is a bet for us."
Petroperu also owns a refinery in the Talara region, which it plans to auction as part of the state company's ongoing piecemeal sell-off.
In the last auction in August, Mobil Corp bought Petroperu's lubricants unit, Petrolube, for $18.9 million.
This sale followed the company's June auctions, when the government sold a 60 percent stake in the La Pampilla refinery near Lima and the rights to develop oil block 8/8X in the northeastern jungle.
A consortium led by Spain's Repsol SA bought the La Pampilla stake for $180.5 million, and a consortium led by Pluspetrol won oil block 8/8X with a bid of $142.2 million.
